title: Use of Point-of-Care Ultrasound in the Prehospital Emergency Medical Service of Saarland: A Prospective Observational Study
summary: Since early 2025, all physician-staffed EMS units in Saarland have been equipped with portable ultrasound devices. In this study, EMS physicians will be anonymously surveyed after missions in which ultrasound was used. The aim is to understand when ultrasound is used, what is found, and whether it influences clinical management (e.g., destination hospital or treatment decisions).
conditions: No single specific disease entity. This is a health services / emergency care topic investigating indications, utilization patterns, and clinical impact of prehospital point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in acute emergency patients treated by EMS.

interventions.name: Prehospital emergency physicians (EMS physicians) in Saarland following missions in which point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) was performed. Prospective, anonymous data collection via a standardized online free-text questionnaire completed immediately after the mission.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Prehospital emergency physicians (EMS physicians) in Saarland (participating EMS physician bases)

POCUS performed during an EMS mission as part of routine care

Willingness to complete the anonymous online questionnaire immediately after the mission (voluntary participation)
Exclusion criteria:
Missions without POCUS performed

Incomplete or clearly duplicate questionnaire entries
